activity_context.topic_title: The Vector Equation of a Line

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $C$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=c+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $c$ is the position vector of $C.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $C(3,2,5)$ and $D(2,1,6)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =⟨2,1,6⟩-⟨3,2,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
